newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-Housing, Philly Fed top data Dec 16 week.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Housing, Philly Fed top data Dec 16 week.

text.p: Projecting a rebound in both housing starts and a key manufacturing survey, U.S. economists said next week's data should reflect moderate economic growth.
On average, 24 economists forecast housing starts rose to a 1.39 million unit annual rate in November after falling off sharply to 1.366 million the month before.
They also projected, on average, that the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia's business outlook survey rose to 7.4 in November from 6.4 in October.
"I would look at housing early in the week, Philly Fed as the week comes to a close," said Kevin Flanagan, vice president and an economist at Dean Witter Reynolds.

Economists said any rise in housing starts would be noteworthy because the figure tends to decline in the colder months. This season appears be an exception, possibly because of the low-interest rate environment, economists said.
"Applications for mortgages seem to be rising," noted Philip Braverman, chief economist at DKB Securities Inc.
Starts data will be released Wednesday at 0830 EST/1330 GMT.
The Philadelphia Fed index, to be released on Thursday, should rise from the previous month amid emerging reports of a rebound in factory activity, economists said.
"The manufacturing indicators have shown signs of firming (and) getting any inventory adjustment behind us," said John Ryding, senior economist at Bear Stearns & Co Inc.
Other data getting a close look next week will be November industrial production, October international trade and a final estimate of third-quarter gross domestic product (GDP).
Survey respondents also projected GDP would not be revised from the previous estimate of 2.0 percent.
